1. Read the two supplied CSV‐style inputs into two DataFrames:
   1a) “borough_stats” with columns borough, avg_no2_value  
   1b) “neighbors” with columns borough, neighbor_list (comma-separated)

2. Handle missing values up-front.  
   • Drop the six rows whose avg_no2_value is NaN; they will play no role in the hotspot test and will not count toward n (data_points_used).  
   • When constructing each borough’s neighbourhood later, ignore any neighbour whose own value is missing (treat its weight wij = 0).

3. After the drop, record data_points_used = 27 (33 rows − 6 missing).

4. Build a Python dict mapping every retained borough i to the set N(i) consisting of i itself plus every neighbour j from the list whose NO2 value is not missing.

5. Compute global reference quantities from the 27 kept boroughs:  
   • n  = 27  
   • X̄ = ( Σ xj ) / n  
   • S  = √[ ( Σ xj² / n ) − X̄² ]

6. For every retained borough i, calculate the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic with binary spatial weights wij = 1 if j ∈ N(i), else 0:  
      Wi      = Σj wij  (size of local area)  
      Σwijxj  = Σj wij xj  
      Σwij²   = Σj wij²  (equals Wi because weights are 0/1)  
      Gi*(i)  = [ Σwijxj − X̄·Wi ] ÷ [ S · √{ [ n·Σwij² − Wi² ] / (n−1) } ]

7. Decision rule (two-tailed):  
   • HOT spot if Gi* ≥ +1.96 (95 % level) and mark as 99 % if Gi* ≥ +2.576  
   • COLD spot if Gi* ≤ −1.96 (95 % level) and mark as 99 % if Gi* ≤ −2.576  
   • Otherwise not significant.

8. Collect every borough that satisfies the rule into a list of formatted strings  
   “BoroughName (HOT, Gi* = <real> )” or “BoroughName (COLD, Gi* = <real> )”.

9. Print:
   • data_points_used = 27  
   • FINAL ANSWER line produced with an f-string as required (or “none” if the list is empty).

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
NO2_PATH = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q1_2023.csv"
ADJ_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(NO2_PATH)          # columns: borough, avg_no2_value
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)         # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Drop rows with missing pollution values
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=["avg_no2_value"]).reset_index(drop=True)
values = df_clean.set_index("borough")["avg_no2_value"]

# Number of boroughs actually used
n = len(values)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build a neighbourhood dictionary (include self)
#    – ignore neighbours that are missing in df_clean
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
neigh_dict = {b: set([b]) for b in values.index}        # start with self

for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, nb = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    # Add both directions if both boroughs have data
    if b in values.index and nb in values.index:
        neigh_dict[b].add(nb)
        neigh_dict[nb].add(b)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Global statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
X_bar = values.mean()
S = np.sqrt((values.pow(2).mean()) - X_bar**2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compute Getis–Ord Gi* for each borough
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
gi_star = {}
for b in values.index:
    neighbours = neigh_dict[b]
    Wi = len(neighbours)                         # Σ w_ij  (binary weights)
    sum_wx = values.loc[list(neighbours)].sum()  # Σ w_ij x_j
    sum_w_sq = Wi                                # Σ w_ij^2 (all 1’s)
    
    numerator = sum_wx - X_bar * Wi
    denominator = S * np.sqrt(((n * sum_w_sq) - (Wi ** 2)) / (n - 1))
    gi_star[b] = numerator / denominator if denominator != 0 else np.nan

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Identify statistically significant hot/cold spots
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
results_strings = []
for b, g in gi_star.items():
    if np.isnan(g):
        continue
    if g >= 2.576:
        results_strings.append(f"{b} (HOT, Gi*={g:.4f})")   # 99% hot
    elif g >= 1.96:
        results_strings.append(f"{b} (HOT, Gi*={g:.4f})")   # 95% hot
    elif g <= -2.576:
        results_strings.append(f"{b} (COLD, Gi*={g:.4f})")  # 99% cold
    elif g <= -1.96:
        results_strings.append(f"{b} (COLD, Gi*={g:.4f})")  # 95% cold

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Print required output
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {n}")

if results_strings:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results_strings)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
